title: Chapter 92: Day and Night 3
content:
Chapter 92

Wei Wuxian let out a silent, weary sigh, a stray thought wandering into his head:Honestly, setting aside all these tangled secrets and hidden motives… I’m far more curious about whether being into dudes is a side effect you can catch through a sacrificial ritual!

Lost in his wandering mind, the grueling exhaustion of the past few days finally caught up with him. He reached up, pressing two fingers hard against his throbbing temples.

Noticing the strain, Lan Wangji spoke softly: "You should rest."

"Alright," Wei Wuxian yielded without a fight. He shuffled over to the room's lone daybed, kicked off his boots, and flopped straight onto his back. "Hanguang-jun, why don't you..."

The words withered in his throat the instant the sheer awkwardness of the situation dawned on him.

There was only one bed in the room. If Lan Wangji wanted to sleep, it meant lying right beside him. Sure, over the past few weeks they had shared a mattress more times than he could count, but ever since Jiang Cheng’s furious tirade in the ancestral hall of Lotus Pier, everything had taken on a desperately fraught, razor-thin tension. Forget asking Lan Wangji to climb in and lie down with him—even that little hesitation over booking rooms downstairs had sent his nerves through a meat grinder.

"No need," Lan Wangji replied quietly.

Wei Wuxian propped himself up on an elbow, reluctant to drop it. "How can you say 'no need'? You've been running on fumes for days, too..."

He instantly regretted opening his mouth. If he pushed the issue and Lan Wangji suddenly decided this living arrangement was entirely too compromising, turning around to demand a separate room after all, wouldn't that make things a hundred times more mortifying?

Lan Wangji’s tone brooked no argument: "I do not require it. Rest."

Rubbing his chin, Wei Wuxian could only mumble, "...Oh. Well, I'll just lie down for a bit, then. Wake me around four, alright?"

Across the room, Lan Wangji sat poised and upright at the wooden table, eyes already closed in quiet, meditative rest. Reassured by the stillness, Wei Wuxian let his body sink back down against the blankets.

Tucking an arm beneath his head, he stared up at the exposed rafters for a while before rolling over, turning his back squarely toward Lan Wangji. Yet after a long, agonizing stretch, his eyes remained wide open. Sleep refused to claim him, and an annoying wave of restlessness began clawing at his chest.

When he’d been putting on that shameless, half-crazed front back then, whining that he could only ever fall asleep with Lan Wangji right next to him, it had obviously been absolute nonsense. Complete fabrication. But somewhere along the way, against all reason, that ridiculous lie had warped into stone-cold reality.

What am I supposed to do now?Wei Wuxian thought, frantic.Am I seriously going to spend the rest of my life entirely unable to sleep unless Lan Zhan is in my bed???

He tossed and turned, wrestling with his own runaway brain, until his heavy eyelids finally surrendered to sleep.

He floated through a thick, dreamless stupor for who knew how many hours. By the time he stirred, the sunlight filtering through the lattice window had long since burned away; judging by the encroaching shadows, it was well past six in the evening.

Wei Wuxian bolted upright. A faint rustle caught his ear, and glancing toward the table, he saw Lan Wangji quietly shutting a book.

"Lan Zhan!" Wei Wuxian gasped. "Why didn't you wake me? Didn't I say four?"

Lan Wangji met his eyes, unhurried. "Restoring your strength and resting your spirit takes priority. There is no rush."

He had crashed and burned for the better part of the day, leaving Lan Wangji sitting alone, probably doing little else besides heading downstairs to fetch something to read. A prickle of guilt stung Wei Wuxian’s ribs. Swinging his legs over the edge, he hopped down. "Sorry about that. My head was totally fried. Why don't you lie down for a bit now?"

"It is nothing," Lan Wangji said.

Right on cue, a brisk knock sounded at the door, followed by the innkeeper's cheery lilt from the hall: "Young masters, your dinner is here!"

Only then did Wei Wuxian realize it was already creeping past seven. Lan Wangji undid the latch, and the landlady breezed inside balancing a heavy tray. Perched neatly on the lacquered wood was a glazed clay jar and a pair of delicate porcelain cups.

"Well, now!" she teased, beaming broadly. "Looks like someone slept straight through the afternoon, didn't they?"

Flushing with sheepish guilt, Wei Wuxian could only muster a strained laugh.

Setting the tray down, she dusted off her apron. "Where are you two traveling in from, anyway? Touring around unfamiliar territory really wears a body out. You've got to take it easy, recharge your batteries, and take your time taking in the sights!"

"Gusu," Wei Wuxian tossed out casually.

Her face lit up. "Figures! No wonder! I knew two boys this strikingly handsome could only come from that gorgeous water country down south!"

Lan Wangji acted as though he were deaf to the world.

Wei Wuxian, on the other hand, let out a booming laugh. "Oh, don't compare me to him—he's got me beat in the looks department by a mile."

"He's classic elegance, you're lively charm," she waved a hand dismissively. "Different styles, but both gorgeous! Oh, speaking of which!" She clapped her hands, eyes sparkling. "If you're out looking for local sights, you really ought to pay a visit to our Guanyin Temple down in the city."

Wei Wuxian had already been looking for an angle to pry about the place, and having her serve it up on a silver platter was a gift. "We actually passed by it earlier today. Seeing a grand Guanyin Temple planted right in the bustling heart of town is quite a rare sight, honestly."

"Tell me about it! Nearly knocked me off my feet when I first laid eyes on it, too."

Wei Wuxian leaned in. "How long have you lived here in Yunping, ma'am?"

"Going on eight years now, give or take."

"Was the temple already standing back then?" he asked. "Did you ever hear why anyone would build a temple right in the middle of a city?"

"Ah, you're asking the wrong lady on that one," she sighed. "Couldn't tell you the history. All I know is the incense burns day and night without stopping. Whenever anyone around here runs into trouble, they run straight to the Bodhisattva to pray for safety. When business is slow, I pop in myself to burn a few sticks."

"Why not take your troubles straight to the local cultivating clan instead?" Wei Wuxian asked, the words tumbling out on pure reflex.

The instant the question left his lips, he caught himself—the dominant cultivation sect governing this entire region was none other than the Yunmeng Jiang Clan.

Sure enough, the landlady’s face soured, her lip curling in distaste. "Go to them? Who'd dare?!"

Wei Wuxian raised an eyebrow. "Oh? Why not?"

"You boys aren't from around here, so you wouldn't know," she lowered her voice, leaning over the table. "Our entire chunk of Yunmeng falls under the Jiang Clan's thumb. That Sect Leader of theirs has a temper like a rabid beast—scares the living daylights out of everyone. His men made it clear ages ago: a clan this size has an enormous territory to watch over, and with nearly a hundred petty poltergeists and minor sprites pulling pranks on common folk every single day, how could they possibly dispatch swordsmen for every tiny headache? Unless someone drops dead, it's not a malevolent haunting. And if it's not a malevolent haunting, we're not supposed to bother them with our petty trifles."

Her indignation flared, huffing: "What kind of backwards logic is that?! Waiting until people are dead before stepping in—isn't that way too late?!"

To be fair, refusing to mobilize unless a crisis involved lethal, high-tier horrors was practically the unspoken industry standard among the prominent sects. The legendary pledge to "venture forth wherever chaos reigns" was sung far and wide as a paragon of virtue, yet throughout the entire cultivation world, the only man who actually lived by that creed was sitting right across from him.

"Besides," the landlady added, shuddering visibly, "Lotus Pier is a waking nightmare! Who'd dare knock on their door?!"

Wei Wuxian dragged his eyes away from Lan Wangji’s serene profile, blinking in mild shock. "Lotus Pier, a nightmare? How on earth could Lotus Pier be scary? Have you actually been?"

"Me? Heaven forbid, no," she spat. "A friend of mine had some nasty haunting at his house and went to beg for help, but his timing was rotten. He walked right in to find Sect Leader Jiang pacing the training grounds, cracking a glowing whip against some poor bastard's skin, thrashing the man until blood and flesh flew everywhere! Screams loud enough to wake the dead! A kind-hearted servant pulled my friend aside and whispered that the Sect Leader had caught the wrong guy again and was in a foul mood, warning him to run before he got caught in the crossfire. My friend dropped his gifts on the dirt and ran for his life, swearing he'd never step foot near that den again."

Wei Wuxian was well aware of the rumors. Over the past decade, Jiang Cheng had scoured the realm, rounding up anyone suspected of using demonic cultivation or seizing bodies, hauling them back to Lotus Pier for brutal interrogation. The poor merchant had clearly walked into Jiang Cheng venting his rabid fury. Imagining the terrifying, twisted snarl on Jiang Cheng's face wasn't hard at all; it was no wonder an ordinary mortal had fled in terror.

"And that's not even all," the landlady piped up again. "I heard another poor soul got chased off, too."

Wei Wuxian rubbed the bridge of his nose. "What scared that one off?" Surely he hadn't walked in on another public whipping. Just how obsessively was Jiang Cheng hunting ghosts, and how often was he lashing out?

"No, no, nothing like that," she clarified. "Just terrible luck, really. The traveler's family name happened to be Wen. And wouldn't you know it, Sect Leader Jiang's sworn mortal enemies share that very same surname! The man has taken out his grudge on every living soul named Wen under the sun. Catches one and he starts grinding his teeth, looking like he wants to peel their skin and snap their tendons on the spot. Never a civil word..."

Wei Wuxian bowed his head, pinching the skin between his brows in suffocating silence.

Fortunately, he didn't need to offer a response. Having rattled off her endless gossip in one breath, the landlady looked thoroughly refreshed. "Aiya, look at me rambling on while your food goes cold! I'll stop bothering you boys and head back down. Just call out if you need anything else!"

Wei Wuxian offered his thanks and saw her to the door. Once it clicked shut, he turned back. "Looks like the trail we're hunting stretches back at least eight years. We'll find a few older locals tomorrow to poke around."

Lan Wangji gave a slight nod.

Wei Wuxian sighed, "Then again, we might come up empty-handed. Eight years is a long time. Plenty of time for a town to forget."

Reaching for the clay jug to pour a drink, his hand hitched in the air for a fraction of a second. He hastily scolded himself beneath his breath:If he doesn't want to drink, drop it. If he does, I'll just ask a couple of harmless questions, nothing more. I just need to figure out what's actually going on in that head of his. Besides, once he sleeps it off, he won't remember a single thing anyway... It won't derail our plans.

Having successfully bribed his own conscience, his hand steadied. He tipped the jug, filling a porcelain cup to the brim, and slid it smoothly in front of Lan Wangji with an easy, casual air. He had fully braced himself for Lan Wangji to wave it away, but perhaps lost in his own quiet thoughts, Lan Wangji didn't even spare the cup a second glance. He raised it to his lips and drained the liquor in a single, unhesitating swallow.

Wei Wuxian brought his own cup up, keeping his eyes locked onto Lan Wangji across the rim. Taking a small, cautious sip, the liquid fire hit his throat so violently he instantly choked, doubling over in a fit of ragged coughs.

Damn,he thought, wheezing,that landlady is a woman of her word! I asked for something with a kick, and she brought pure liquid dynamite.

Truth be told, he had tossed back spirits ten times stronger than this in his past life without batting an eye. Getting caught off guard now was entirely the fault of his wandering, frantic mind.

Wiping a stray splash of liquor from his sleeve, he glanced back up.

Right on cue, Lan Wangji had slipped completely into his familiar drunken stupor.

This time, the alcohol had dropped him right where he sat. He remained rigidly upright upon the woven mat, posture immaculate, his eyes shut and chin tipped downward just a fraction—indistinguishable from his everyday meditation.

Wei Wuxian waved a hand back and forth in front of his face. Not a twitch.

Reassured, a cheeky grin cracked across his face. Reaching out with gentle fingers, he lightly hooked Lan Wangji’s chin, crooning in a hushed murmur, "These past few days have been absolute agony, you know. Hanguang-jun, you've finally fallen right into my hands."

Deep in his drunken slumber, Lan Wangji tilted his face up with astonishing docility.

When those pale, icy eyes were open, the man carried an untouchable, frosty aura that felt entirely unapproachable. But with his lashes resting against his cheeks, the severe lines of his face softened into something breathtakingly gentle—looking for all the world like an exquisite, peerless statue of carved jade, quiet and serene, radiating a magnetic pull that was almost unfair.

The longer Wei Wuxian stared, the more hopelessly captivated he became. Unable to help himself, he cradled the man's jaw, leaning in closer... closer... until the distance between them turned dangerously intimate.

The cool, familiar drift of sandalwood snapped his senses back like a splash of freezing water.

Abort! Bad idea!

Panic seizing him, Wei Wuxian yanked his hands back. Deprived of support, Lan Wangji’s head dropped back onto his chest with a soft bob.

Wei Wuxian’s heart was hammering against his ribs like a trapped bird. Desperate to shake off the feverish heat buzzing in his ears, he dropped to the floorboards and rolled back and forth across the rug, springing to his feet to chant silent mantras of calm under his breath. Shuffling back to his seat, he sat cross-legged across from the sleeping beauty, trying his best to look dignified.

He waited for him to wake up.

Yet his mischievous itch refused to die. Creeping his hand across the table, he reached out and poked Lan Wangji’s cheek.

Once. Twice.

A sudden realization struck him: in all the years they had crossed paths, he had never once seen Lan Wangji smile.

Curiosity winning out, Wei Wuxian placed his index fingers against the corners of Lan Wangji’s lips, gently tugging them upward to see what a smile looked like on that ethereal face.

A sharp, sudden sting pinched his finger.

Lan Wangji’s golden eyes snapped wide, staring dead at him with an icy, piercing glare.

And Wei Wuxian’s index finger was clamped firmly between his teeth.
